name: Marxist humanism
summary: Marxist humanism reads Marx through his early writings on alienation, treating socialism as the overcoming of estrangement so that people regain control of their own creative activity. It stresses human agency, ethics and praxis against economic determinism and Soviet dialectical materialism, and rejects Stalinism, vanguard-party rule and state capitalism in favor of workers' self-management and participatory democracy. It remains anti-capitalist, critical of consumerism and of private property as self-estrangement.
scope: The mid-twentieth-century current that grew after the 1932 publication of Marx's 1844 Manuscripts: Fromm, the Johnson-Forest Tendency (James, Dunayevskaya), the Yugoslav Praxis School (Petrovic, Markovic) and Eastern European revisionists, with Lukacs, Lefebvre and Sartre as influences. Excludes Leninist and Althusserian structuralist readings. Positions on modern social issues are mostly inferred and low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Erich Fromm
keyFigures.role: Psychoanalyst who gave a widely read humanist account of Marx's concept of alienation.

keyFigures.name: Raya Dunayevskaya
keyFigures.role: Johnson-Forest Tendency co-founder who analysed the USSR as state capitalism and opposed vanguardism.

keyFigures.name: Gajo Petrovic
keyFigures.role: Leading philosopher of the Yugoslav Praxis School.

sources.usedFor: Humanist critique of Stalinism and party elites, self-management, free speech.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Needs-based, de-alienated socialism implies guaranteed basic care, though the sources do not discuss healthcare policy specifically.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred: adherents back worker welfare, but see wage labor itself as the problem and reforms as secondary.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Fromm holds that capitalist markets manufacture needs and make people servants of what they produce, yet he equally rejects a state acting as employer, so the answer is a mild no.

public-ownership.rationale: Social ownership follows from abolishing private property, but Fromm warns a bureaucratic state employer reproduces alienation, so support is for democratic public control.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian aims; taxation is a reformist tool humanists rarely discuss.

unions-good.rationale: Workers' self-activity and organization are central to the Johnson-Forest and Praxis traditions, though adherents criticize bureaucratized unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Marx's 1844 text calls private property human self-estrangement and communism its positive abolition.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred: adherents want corporate power curbed, but regard regulation as insufficient to end alienation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Cutting provision for needs contradicts the aim of social conditions for human flourishing; dependency arguments are not part of the tradition.

worker-ownership.rationale: Workers' control and self-management are named as the humanist alternative to both capitalism and party-state bureaucracy.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the Praxis emphasis on freedom of speech and individual dignity against state power.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the stress on individual autonomy; drug policy is not discussed in the sources.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Praxis theorists demanded freedom of speech and press in East and West, which suggests wariness of legal speech restrictions.

strong-leader.rationale: The movement arose against Stalinist leader worship and favors participatory democracy from below.

state-harmful.rationale: Fromm's vision aligns with Marx's eventual stateless society, but a typical adherent does not call the state simply harmful now.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from humanist concern with violence and security; not discussed in the sources.

empower-police-military.rationale: Humanists oppose coercive state apparatus and bureaucratic power; funding for it is not their program.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Marx's 1844 text treats the reduction of people to commodities critically, while autonomy arguments pull the other way; adherents split.

decide-locally.rationale: Self-management and decentralized participatory socialism favor local decision-making, though not as an absolute rule.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from a humanist view that character is formed by social conditions.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred: humanists do not treat inherited family forms as foundation, favoring free development of persons.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on human freedom and flourishing; anachronistic for early thinkers.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from autonomy and the emphasis on human subjects' control over their lives.

more-religion-public.rationale: Marx's text treats religion as estrangement; humanists such as Garaudy sought dialogue but did not want religion enlarged in public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from universal emancipation aims; racial issues are not central in the sources used.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the view that human nature is largely shaped historically and socially.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Fromm stresses liberation of all humanity; national traditions are not a value in the sources.

gradual-change.rationale: De-alienation requires radical social transformation and revolution, not respect for established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from universal humanism and Marx's liberation of all people rather than one nation.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Internationalist in spirit but suspicious of bureaucracies of states; adherents are split and sources are silent.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred: a market-driven world economy that subjects people to impersonal forces is part of what they criticize.

nation-first.rationale: Fromm and Marx stress the whole species and all people, so national self-interest above cooperation is rejected.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Adherents are split between anti-imperialism and concern for human rights; sources do not address it.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from universal humanism and internationalism; not directly discussed.

limit-growth.rationale: Fromm criticizes consumerism but the sources do not address ecological limits to growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred: humanity governed by its own creations is a standing theme; climate was not an issue for the founders.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Fromm cites nuclear weapons and bureaucracy as human creations ruling humanity, so technology alone does not solve problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from Fromm's wariness of nuclear technology as an alienated creation.

revolution-justified.rationale: Socialist revolution is held to be the realization of philosophy, though adherents stress its humane, self-activating character.

experts-over-public.rationale: Participatory democracy and workers' control reject rule by specialists or party elites.

central-planning.rationale: Fromm rejects the state as capitalist employer, and the movement opposes Soviet-style command planning, though planning as such is not rejected.

socialized-markets.rationale: Praxis theorists defended worker self-management in the Yugoslav economy, which included markets, but the sources do not settle the point.

land-value-tax.rationale: Georgist single-tax reform keeps private land rent and property, which Marx's 1844 text sees as estrangement.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from opposition to private property and accumulation of wealth.

basic-income.rationale: Adherents might welcome decoupling needs from wage work but see it as insufficient; sources are silent.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred: internationalist humanism sees protectionism as nationalist, though adherents are not committed free traders.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Fromm opposes the state as capitalist, yet adherents accept public control of the economy; split and inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Marx's 1844 text aims at abolishing private property, not spreading it, though it also condemns crude levelling.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Overcoming estranged labor and the sense of having implies ending wage labor and money relations as the aim of communism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred: leaving money to the market conflicts with critique of market domination.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies imposed from above conflict with self-management from below.

one-party-rule.rationale: Eastern European humanist revisionists and Praxis theorists opposed party monopoly and demanded free speech and democratic socialism.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary authority conflicts with universal human emancipation and self-rule.

democracy-best.rationale: Humanists back democracy, though in a participatory, workers' control form rather than liberal procedure only.

direct-votes.rationale: Direct democracy and participation are favored over party and representative mediation.

workers-councils.rationale: The Johnson-Forest tendency backed workers' self-management and direct democracy over parties, which matches councils as power base.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred from self-determination and opposition to enforced party-state unity.

natural-rulers.rationale: Marx and Fromm's liberation of all people rejects natural hierarchies of rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Revolution is defended as the realization of philosophy; Merleau-Ponty justified revolutionary violence by consequences before reconsidering.

war-builds-character.rationale: Fromm's humanism holds nothing in war develops human creativity; he warns of nuclear arms.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred from Marx's treatment of religion as estrangement; Garaudy sought dialogue, not state religion.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Marx's 1844 text treats religious estrangement as a form of alienation, so scripture-based law runs counter.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Privatizing justice and defense extends private property into core public functions.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from universal humanism and Fromm's warnings about nuclear arms.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Fromm and Marx emphasize human universality and liberation of all people.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class conflict remains central, but humanists reject economic determinism and stress human agency and praxis.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Marx's 1844 text opposes crude levelling-down but aims at material equality enabling a rich human life.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from anti-colonial strands (Fanon, James) and opposition to dispossession.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from anti-colonial strands associated with the tradition.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from universal species-wide humanism over civilizational blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Marx's 1844 text says private property reduces human senses to the sense of having.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Praxis thinkers stress individual dignity, autonomy and free critique against party demands.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Marx's 1844 text calls communism fully developed naturalism and humanism, treating nature as part of human life, not merely a resource.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred: poverty is blamed on social institutions, not population, and coercive limits clash with humanism.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Fromm criticizes alienation in industrial society but sees history as also a development of human capacities.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Fromm warns technology can enslave humans to their creations.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not discussed; humanists value human development but fear technology controlling people.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Fromm's analysis of bureaucracy and human beings ruled by their own creations opposes handing decisions to systems.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the stress on freedom against state power.

restore-past-order.rationale: Humanism aims at future de-alienation through radical change, not restoring a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The tradition is deeply philosophical and holds theory and practice to be united, so results alone are not the test.

direct-action.rationale: Worker self-activity and praxis are emphasized over party and parliamentary mediation.

means-match-ends.rationale: Humanists criticized Stalinist methods and joined practice to humanist aims of revolutionary change.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Fromm sees history as growth of human capacities alongside alienation, with the answer lying forward.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Marx's 1844 text discusses the division of labor as part of estranged activity; full abolition is a distant aim.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Marx's 1844 text describes the rich human being as one with many needs and human wealth defined by need, not by having.

production-for-use.rationale: Fromm opposes manufactured needs and production aimed at profit rather than human development.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Humanists hold early alienation themes underlie Marx's later economic analysis in Capital.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Praxis and Johnson-Forest thinkers rejected party dictatorship; some accept Marx's phrase in democratic sense.

collective-farming.rationale: Inferred from opposition to enforced collectivization under Stalinism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Fromm links militarism and nuclear arms to alienation, but the sources do not state an inevitability thesis.

taxation-theft.rationale: Rejecting private property as estrangement, adherents cannot call taxes theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Praxis stresses free expression but sources do not take up the harm principle.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Praxis emphasizes individual dignity, yet adherents see persons as social beings, not isolated rights-holders.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from Fromm's wariness of the state's coercive power over persons.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Humanists stress participation and democratic control over exit as a safeguard.

state-as-business.rationale: Fromm explicitly criticizes the state as capitalist employer and customers as passive consumers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Marx's 1844 text ties freedom to material conditions that make senses and capacities fully human.

media-academia-power.rationale: Inferred: the tradition places power in capital and bureaucracy, not intellectual institutions.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Humanism holds human character is shaped by social conditions and is universal.

organic-representation.rationale: Inferred: they prefer workers' councils and participation, not corporative bodies tied to family and community hierarchy.

total-state.rationale: Praxis thinkers opposed party-state control over culture and demanded free speech.

national-rebirth.rationale: Humanism's universalism has no place for nation-centered rebirth myths.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and humanist opposition to domination.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal bonds contradict the aim of free, self-determining persons.

bound-labor.rationale: Bound labor is a form of estranged labor that Marx's 1844 text condemns.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Marxist humanists see ideas as tied to praxis and class position, but Praxis also upholds free critique and truth-seeking.

universal-morality.rationale: Humanists emphasize ethics and human nature as a basis for Marx's critique, though not as ahistorical moral law.

single-common-good.rationale: Class conflict remains real; an undifferentiated common good is not the humanist starting point.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Adherents divided on Zionism and national statehood; the sources do not address it.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not discussed; adherents split on nation-based rights.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; neither endorsed nor opposed by the core of the tradition.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers' control and self-management are core humanist proposals.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred: marketizing education conflicts with opposition to commodification.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred: austerity priority is not part of the tradition's concerns, which favor public provision.

economic-freedom.rationale: Marx's 1844 text sees private property as estranging, so economic freedom as property rights is not a condition of freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred: humanists favor democratic institutions rather than reliance on rulers' virtue.

national-self-determination.rationale: Inferred from anti-colonial strands; humanists generally back peoples' right of self-rule.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred from Fromm's warnings about militarism.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Fromm values reason yet insists on feeling and productive love, and he reinterprets religion rather than dismissing it.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from universal humanism rejecting citizenship-based exclusion.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Work under capitalism is estranged labor, so compelling it is rejected.

class-collaboration.rationale: Humanists regard capitalist employer-worker relations as exploitative and reject partnership as an ideal.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Marx's 1844 text treats human culture as accumulated human essence to be reclaimed, not destroyed.

dominated-front.rationale: Not discussed; mixed views among anti-colonial strands.

workers-nation.rationale: Marxists understand the working class as international, and humanists as universal.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from emancipation of all people and free development of every individual.

ban-interest.rationale: Not discussed; humanists prefer abolishing capitalist relations over banning interest alone.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Contradicts the aim of liberating all people.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marx's account of state as class domination is inherited, though humanists stress human agency over mechanical models.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from criticism of unlimited production and consumption.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no place in a humanist critique of social structure. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred: fairer representation is compatible with democratic aims, though not their main demand.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from emancipatory aims and Lefebvre's extension of alienation beyond labor.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Praxis theorists attacked party-elite bureaucracy as self-serving, but the claim is broader than their argument.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics contradicts human dignity and equal worth central to humanism.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from Praxis demands for freedom and the victims of Stalinist repression.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Protecting property and nothing more defends what Marx calls self-estrangement.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Fromm says Marx aimed at liberation of all people, not one class.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Adherents split, including Johnson-Forest and Praxis; the sources do not state a position.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Conflicts with freedom of conscience emphasized by Praxis.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred: religious-cultural bans are not a humanist program.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from Marx's treatment of religion as estrangement.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Praxis rejected Stalinist apologetics shaped to the needs of the party elite.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Participatory democracy implies legitimacy from those governed.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist national goals conflict with universal humanist aims.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Revolution is defended, so an absolute ban on initiating force is rejected, though humanists dislike violence.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Fromm sees capitalist competition as a source of alienation, not human development.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Praxis stressed free speech; banning parties conflicts but Eastern bloc humanists accepted anti-fascist restrictions.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Marx's 1844 text treats domination of workers by property as unfreedom beyond actual interference.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed; adherents want direct democracy but value checks against party power.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Johnson-Forest Tendency rejected Leninist vanguardism in favor of workers' self-activity.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Marx's 1844 text sees poverty as expression of estrangement, and communism meets human needs first.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Extending private ownership conflicts with abolishing private property, though adherents may support tenants.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Workers' self-activity is central to the tradition.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Fromm and Marx locate causes in social institutions and relations of production.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Participatory ideals could support it, but it is not discussed in the sources.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Praxis theorists demanded civil liberties against party-state emergency claims.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from priority on human needs.

party-controls-media.rationale: Praxis theorists demanded freedom of speech and press in East and West.

party-commands-army.rationale: Opposed party-state apparatus controlling coercive power; democratic control is favored.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred from workers' control and anti-elite democracy; Commune-style ideas are not discussed in sources.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Praxis thinkers opposed enforced party line, though many accept organization.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Internationalist leaning but sources do not discuss the EU.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Concentrating command in a head of state contradicts participatory democracy.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not a humanist concern; the preference is for non-hierarchical self-organization.

clerical-rule.rationale: Religious estrangement as treated by Marx makes clerical rule unacceptable.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and Fromm's anti-militarism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Praxis thinkers demanded free expression and ruthless criticism.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from participatory democracy skeptical of entrenched leaders.

recall-officials.rationale: Direct participation implies popular control over officials.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Inferred from Fromm's critique of militarism and nuclear arms.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Universal ownership of housing is not a humanist aim, which targets alienation, not tenure form.

people-in-arms.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's preference for popular self-activity over standing apparatus.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Inferred: no romanticization of rural life; Fromm sees progress through development.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Tradition's thinkers are intellectuals who reject anti-intellectualism.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred from universal humanism and rejection of hierarchies among peoples.

death-penalty.rationale: Fromm's humanism treats execution as incompatible with human dignity. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Marx's 1844 text and the movement's naturalism reject religious doctrine as science.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Marx's 1844 text links commodification of senses to private property while free-expression views pull the other way.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from Praxis defense of free expression and dignity.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not discussed; adherents split between tolerance and secularism.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Humanists value free development of individuality.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from anti-colonial and anti-capitalist commitments.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: political liberation without removing estrangement is incomplete.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Praxis theorists demanded civil liberties against party-state justifications.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Fromm cites nuclear weapons as humanity ruled by its own creations. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; adherents prefer participatory structures to executives.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Inferred from democratic control over the economy.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and peace emphasis.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: A weaker form of the Marxist position that private property estranges people; adherents want it abolished.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Johnson-Forest Tendency called the USSR bureaucratic state capitalism, and Fromm says a state employer is still capitalist.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from Fromm's concern about technology controlling humanity.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from anti-militarism and critique of military blocs.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from opposition to the Soviet suppression of Hungary and general anti-imperialism.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Adherents wary of both clerical power and state coercion; sources silent.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not a humanist concern; ceremonial heads are not valued.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from opposition to enforced party-state unity.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Marx's 1844 text treats religious estrangement as illusion, and rulers' sacredness as alienation.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Regressive redistribution conflicts with the egalitarian aim. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

character-from-environment.rationale: Fromm describes Marx as seeing man's nature as developed historically through social conditions, though not blank.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Opposed to party elites above law; Praxis demanded freedoms.

space-expansion.rationale: Not a humanist aim and Fromm warns about technology's ends.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred: they favor participatory democracy, not rule by few.

leader-cult.rationale: Khrushchev's 1956 denunciation of Stalin galvanized the movement's critics of personality cult.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Johnson-Forest view that Soviet bureaucracy reproduced class rule fits the claim, though Praxis views vary.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred from abolishing private property and democratic ownership by producers.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Conflicts with freedom of conscience. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

women-must-cover.rationale: Conflicts with individual autonomy and dignity. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

common-currency.rationale: The sources never discuss monetary unions; internationalism and distrust of money power leave adherents with no settled view.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred from universal over ethnic-linguistic unity.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The movement rejects economic determinism and Soviet dialectical materialism in favor of human agency, though material conditions still matter.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not addressed; neither the competition nor the cartel is defended.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred: bailouts socialize losses for capitalists, but adherents mostly want a different economy.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred from participatory democracy yet commitment to free expression and rights.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from labor protection and anti-alienation concerns.

moral-incentives.rationale: Fromm hopes for work as free creative activity rather than reward-driven; moral incentives fit but were not discussed.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Rejects vanguard substitution for workers' own activity.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Equality of human worth rejects hereditary privilege.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Contradicts universal liberation of all people.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from democratic control over the economy.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Marx-inspired crisis theory; though Fromm sees alienation persisting, humanists focus less on collapse.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Praxis demanded entrenched civil liberties against the party-state.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: democratic decision-making binding on all.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from Praxis defense of freedom against arbitrary power.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Humanists prefer participatory bodies to parliaments, yet value over monarchy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from naturalism that treats humans as part of nature.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Marx's naturalism places humans within nature, but the sources say nothing on animal farming or research, so adherents have no settled view.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Charity by privileged is not the aim; abolishing privilege is.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Praxis and political commitment are defining for the tradition.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Lefebvre extended alienation to consumerism and culture; Fromm describes passive consumers.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramsci's philosophy of praxis, counted among precursors, emphasizes consent and culture.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from anti-colonial and Marxist economic analysis.

native-born-offices.rationale: Contradicts universal humanism. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

party-own-road.rationale: Praxis thinkers resisted Yugoslav party orthodoxy and sought authentic Marxism, opposing direction from above.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The sources do not address development strategy; internationalist solidarity pulls toward aid while anti-imperialism pulls toward self-reliance.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Humanists condemn Stalinism but still distinguish Marx's goals from fascism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Humanist and Marxist history takes slavery as central. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from anti-racist and anti-Stalinist commitments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Nothing in the sources bears on gendered education or health gaps; adherents would likely favor attention to all disadvantage without a fixed line.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The sources do not address domestic violence statistics or services; adherents' views would divide along feminist and universalist lines.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Not addressed; universal humanism pulls against, anti-imperialism toward.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from Lefebvre-style extensions of alienation and labor critique.

filial-duty.rationale: The sources are silent on family obligations; humanist stress on free individuals and on mutual care pulls in opposite directions.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from participatory democracy against bureaucratic rule.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The sources do not discuss investment screening; adherents oppose capital's power but are not economic nationalists.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on individual freedom.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Direct democracy and workers' control imply recallable delegates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Privatizing social provision runs against social solidarity. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Marx's 1844 text opposes private property in land but the sources do not endorse use-based tenure, so adherents have no settled view.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary budget control is not addressed in the sources; adherents favor popular control but prefer participatory bodies to parliaments.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The sources never address legal tests of discrimination; adherents oppose racism but would divide on this legal doctrine.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Fromm says under alienation needs are manufactured and people become passive consumers of what weakens them.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from anti-militarism and anti-Stalinist stance.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The Soviet suppression of the Hungarian uprising in 1956 galvanized humanist critics.

corporate-influence.rationale: Marx's critique of capital as domination of people by property makes corporate influence part of the alienation.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from freedom of expression stress.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The sources say nothing on birth policy; adherents oppose nationalist demography but support family provision, leaving the answer unsettled.

residents-only-property.rationale: The sources do not discuss local housing restrictions; solidarity with newcomers conflicts with local democratic control.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on meaningful work and needs.

democratic-peace.rationale: The sources do not discuss this empirical thesis; adherents attribute war to economic and bureaucratic structures, not regime type alone.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The sources do not take up political obligation; adherents reject the state's claim to authority but also value democratic legitimacy.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The sources do not address marriage law; Marx's critique of bourgeois family is not developed in the cited texts, leaving adherents split.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Praxis demanded freedom of the press and open critique.

local-production.rationale: The sources do not discuss localism in production; decentralized participatory socialism favors it, while internationalism favors exchange.

informal-organisation.rationale: Dunayevskaya and James stressed spontaneity and self-activity, but they did not reject organization.

religious-nation.rationale: Marx's 1844 text treats religion as estrangement.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism and universal equality.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Marx's 1844 text opposes crude communism that levels everything; personal possession is retained apart from means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Humanists see themselves as communists in Marx's sense, while critiquing Soviet version.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from opposing commodification of needs.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marx's 1844 text treats religious estrangement as a form of consciousness mirrored in real estrangement, though Fromm reinterprets religion more sympathetically.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Fromm describes history as growing human development alongside alienation.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from Lefebvre-style extension and universal emancipation.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Contradicts universal humanism. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Fromm's decentralized participatory socialism fits small communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: Contradicts universal humanism. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Fromm rejects both capitalism and Soviet statism while claiming Marx's communism, so a third-course framing is contested.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Contradicts humanist commitment to truth and dignity. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Conflicts with Praxis demands for freedom and dignity. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Praxis demanded freedom of speech and press and opposed party-state suppression of critique.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Conflicts with Praxis stress on free critique.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Religious obligations of this kind are not part of the tradition.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Religious law as authority is rejected.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Humanists favor participatory democracy and workers' control, and Fromm advocates decentralized participatory socialism.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred from universal emancipation beyond class alone; Fromm stresses liberation of all people.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Marxist humanism sits firmly on the left in tradition and class analysis. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marx's 1844 manuscripts on estranged labor are the founding text of the movement.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Contradicts universal humanism. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Marx's 1844 text treats religion as estrangement.

social-market-economy.rationale: Fromm rejects capitalism, though social protection is welcomed as partial.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred from anti-militarism and Fromm's nuclear warnings.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Humanists criticized both Soviet and Western blocs.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred from cooperative and democratic ownership.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from priority on human needs.

property-franchise.rationale: Property qualifications contradict democratic and egalitarian aims.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Humanism holds that conflict arises from social and economic structures, not from ethnic or racial difference.

reification.rationale: Reification, developed by Lukacs, is described as a central theme of Marxist humanism and is not captured by the existing alienation statement.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred from the early Marx's view of nature as humanity's "inorganic body" and the stress on overcoming estrangement; later ecofeminist links are not discussed in the sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist critique that formal freedoms are hollow under private property and from the humanist stress on real, not merely formal, self-determination.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from the Praxis School's opposition to arbitrary party-state rule and its call for self-managing, accountable institutions.

racial-franchise.rationale: Marxist humanism's universal concept of human nature and its rejection of Stalinist and nationalist exclusion make a racial franchise incompatible with its core.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the current's support for participatory democracy and workers' self-management, which favours any means of wider direct participation.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the Praxis School's call for democratic accountability against bureaucratic secrecy; the sources do not discuss records policy.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: A humanism built on free, self-determined human relations opposes state restrictions on whom people may marry.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Targeting people by religion contradicts the universal, anti-estrangement humanism at the current's core.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on direct, participatory self-government; sortition itself is not discussed in the sources.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred from Fromm's humanistic reading of religious tradition and the current's view of religion as an expression of alienation to be reasoned through; not directly sourced.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Marx's 1844 Manuscripts, central to the current, treat accumulation of private property as estranging and dominating human beings; extended here to freedom.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the current's emphasis on human dignity and emancipation; the sources do not discuss military service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: humanists criticize Soviet-style state imposition and favor freedom of conscience, though Marx viewed religion as alienation.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: the current opposes the coercive state and its Stalinist form but no source takes a position on abolishing police and prisons.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred: the current favors workers' self-management and democratic control, not communal quotas in executive power; not discussed.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred: de-alienated socialism rests on social provision and workers' control rather than charity, which the 1844 Manuscripts criticize.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; Praxis School stresses self-management and direct participation, which is neutral on term limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from the current's support for self-management and participatory democracy, though delegation is not discussed.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred: the current's focus is alienation and social transformation, and existential risk is not discussed.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the current's emphasis on human emancipation and equality; religious offices are not discussed.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on overcoming domination in human relations; Marx's 1844 Manuscripts treat the man-woman relation as a measure of human development.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from its internationalist, anti-nationalist socialism, which cares about people's share in decisions where they live.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from its needs-based, anti-commodity view of human life; housing policy is not discussed.

abolish-ip.rationale: Marx's critique of private property is not applied to patents or copyright in the sources.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Praxis critique of party elites and regimentation implies opposition to state-run drilled youth organisations.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to militarism and Cold War blocs; not discussed in the sources.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from its anti-imperialist socialism; not discussed in the sources.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from its humanist ethics, which condemn the destruction of human beings; not discussed.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Marx's 1844 Manuscripts treat private property as self-estrangement and labour as the human creative activity, so income should follow work rather than ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: it rejects Soviet pacifism-versus-violence dogma and does not hold an absolute ban on killing.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: It sees nations as historical products; inferred from its historical-materialist roots.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The sources do not address the question; humanist readings stress human nature, but adherents are split.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents are split between class-based and identity-based approaches.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from its secular humanism and rejection of cults of sacrifice.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Marx treats religion as a product of alienation and the humanists keep the materialist view of politics as human interests and praxis.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The sources are silent on diaspora and homelands.

culture-before-state.rationale: Culture and the state are not ranked in the sources.

god-not-male.rationale: Marxist humanists are secular and the question is not addressed in the sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; some humanists value religious ethics, others reject religion.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from its internationalism and view of socialism as liberation of all people, not one national group.

independent-unions.rationale: Marxist humanists criticise party and state elites controlling workers and favour workers' self-management, which implies organisations answering to workers themselves.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Marxist humanism rejects Stalinism and state capitalism, holding that state ownership under a ruling elite is not socialism; Fromm stresses socialism as liberation of all.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from its anti-capitalism and support for social ownership; the sources do not discuss local services specifically.

second-chamber.rationale: Legislative design is not discussed; the current favours self-management over parliamentary forms.

municipal-property.rationale: The Praxis School favoured social self-management, but sources do not say whether ownership should be local, so this is genuinely open.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Self-management and participatory democracy are stressed, but confederal structures specifically are not discussed in the sources.

family-wage.rationale: Wage-setting for households is not addressed; Marx's critique of wage labour as alienated points away from both options.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Medical regulation is not addressed by the current.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Ageing research is not addressed; nothing in the sources suggests a view either way.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from its egalitarian, anti-capitalist stance, which favours public oversight of the economy, though privacy against state surveillance cuts the other way.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the current's emphasis on free speech and critique of bureaucratic control, as in the Praxis School; online anonymity itself is anachronistic.

person-over-state.rationale: Marxist humanism centres the individual's self-realisation and attacks regimes treating people as means; Fromm describes socialism as liberating the person.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Marx's 1844 text treats religion as a form of alienation, yet Fromm stresses a rich inner life; adherents are split on spiritual needs.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Regional self-government is not discussed in the sources.

gm-crops.rationale: Genetically engineered crops are not addressed by the current.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban density is not addressed; Lefebvre wrote on cities but the sources do not state this view.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred from its universal humanist socialism, which treats class and common humanity as the basis for organising rather than race.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from its universalist view of humanity and hostility to nationalism and ethnic identity; not discussed directly.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from its anti-militarist, anti-nationalist stance (it rejects war and military superiority); sources do not state this directly.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Marxist humanists stress internationalism and human community over national categories, so a language-based nation concept is mildly rejected; inferred, not discussed in the sources.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the humanist insistence on a universal human community and on democratic equality over communal divisions; the sources do not address electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from the Praxis School's critique of nationalism and party-state propaganda; the sources do not discuss claims of foreign plots.

free-public-college.rationale: Education as free development of human capacities and a needs-based, de-alienated socialism imply free public higher education, though the sources do not discuss tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Pricing pollution leaves market logic and commodity relations in place, which humanists criticise; inferred, and adherents may accept it as a tool.

future-generations.rationale: Fromm and Marx treat nature and human development as a shared inheritance that estranged production destroys; the duty is inferred, not stated in the sources.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Humanists value care and cooperation but also reject fixed essences of human nature by sex; Dunayevskaya's women's-liberation work points both ways, so adherents are split.

arms-reduction.rationale: Humanists oppose militarism and the Cold War blocs, and Praxis thinkers criticised state power and arms build-ups; disarmament follows from core principles, though the sources do not state it directly.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Opposition to bureaucratic elites deciding in secret and demand for democratic control imply open diplomacy; inferred, not discussed in the sources.

capital-controls.rationale: Anti-capitalist and self-managing economy implies social control over capital movements, but humanists focused on alienation rather than finance; inferred.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Arms control is not discussed; the tradition opposes state coercion but also vanguard militias, so it is left split.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from its stress on human agency and ethics over state authority; Praxis School thinkers criticised state power but did not take an explicit stance on conscientious refusal.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Its self-management and participatory socialism supports workers organising collectively to set conditions, as the Praxis School and Johnson-Forest tendency stressed workers' own organisation.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credits are not addressed; the tradition seeks to overcome wage labour and would regard them as palliatives, but adherents may still back them.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to capitalist constraint of human needs and favour of democratic control over the economy; fiscal rules are not addressed.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from its anti-capitalist, internationalist outlook; not addressed in the sources.

smash-state-machine.rationale: It opposes state-capitalist bureaucracy but stresses self-management and democratic participation; the question of smashing or using the state is not addressed in the sources.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Its Yugoslav Praxis strand backed workers' self-management and pluralism over a Soviet-style blueprint.

nature-as-capital.rationale: It holds that nature and human needs have value apart from the market and criticises treating things as commodities, though it did not discuss natural capital accounting. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

sacred-nation.rationale: Humanist Marxism is secular and internationalist and rejects treating nation or other abstractions as sacred above the individual; inferred from its critique of alienation.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from its concern for overcoming the estrangement imposed by private property; student loans are not addressed.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from its anti-capitalist critique of exploitation and unequal development; not addressed in the sources.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Fromm and Marx's 1844 manuscripts ground the critique of alienation in a human essence and its needs, though not as something sacred; adherents also stress that humans create themselves historically.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from its support for free expression and democratic participation (Praxis School free speech), though public broadcasting is not discussed.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred: Marx's 1844 writings treat religion as a form of alienation, which this current follows, though Fromm himself drew on religious traditions.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred: de-alienated socialism favours security for working producers, including farmers, but the sources do not discuss farm policy.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the current's humanist and antimilitarist ethics, though the sources do not discuss nuclear arms.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred: the Praxis School and Johnson-Forest Tendency rejected vanguard parties but backed independent working-class organisation; the sources do not address a workers' party directly.

ban-fgm.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the current's humanist concern for human dignity and bodily freedom.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: A humanist reading of Marx that aims at the full development of every person implies equal property and inheritance rights for women, though the sources do not state it.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred: the current favours democratic social control over the economy and would not leave pollution to private suits alone.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: the current stresses workers' self-management and participatory democracy over customary authority.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred: the critique of alienation and consumerism implies priority for human flourishing over unlimited private choice, though the sources do not discuss this.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred: humanist ethics and the view of crime as arising from alienation favour individualised treatment over fixed sentences.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents could differ.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Marxist humanists back workers' organisation and self-management, but compulsory membership is not discussed in the sources.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from the stress on broad popular participation; barriers to voting are not discussed in the sources.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the humanist view of religion as a form of alienation to be overcome without coercion, and from a secular socialist state; not discussed directly.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Praxis School and Marxist humanists criticise party-state rule and call for workers' self-management, so elections alone do not make a government democratic.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from Fromm's view of free, loving relationships and rejection of repressive moral codes; not stated for this issue.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on human freedom and rejection of Soviet-style state control; the internet is anachronistic for most sources.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Adherents are likely split on a negative income tax: it fits a human-centred minimum income, but replaces welfare institutions with a market-style scheme; not discussed in the sources.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from the core aim of full human emancipation and equal agency for all; women's suffrage is not discussed in the sources.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Marx's early writings treat religion as a form of alienation, but the sources do not single out its effect on women, and adherents are split; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the humanist rejection of fixed human nature and biological determinism; race is not discussed in the sources.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Adherents favour women's emancipation, but the movement distrusts state bureaucracy; the sources do not address dedicated agencies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Marx's 1844 Manuscripts treat private property as the expression of estranged labour, so a claim to ownership by first appropriation is rejected.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred: humanist ethics and anti-militarism favour accountability for atrocities, though the sources never address international tribunals and adherents distrust great-power justice.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Marxist humanism stresses human self-creation and critical, secular ethics; inferred from its rejection of dogma, including Soviet orthodoxy, so the sources do not address scripture directly.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on overcoming all forms of alienation and on full human emancipation; the sources do not discuss Indigenous self-government.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Praxis School and Johnson-Forest adherents rejected bureaucratic Soviet-type states as state capitalism or Stalinism, so they would not defend a bureaucracy-ruled planned state, though some opposed capitalist restoration. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

indirect-election.rationale: Praxis thinkers and Dunayevskaya stressed direct self-management, but the workers' councils they praised send delegates upward, which is exactly this layered election; their position on it is mixed.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the humanist critique of religion as alienation in the 1844 Manuscripts and the rejection of privileged institutions; no source addresses church status.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to self-management and decentralised control; the sources do not discuss ethnic autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the stress on popular self-determination and participation; the sources do not discuss territorial disputes.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: adherents opposed nationalism and imperialism but nothing in the sources addresses colonial borders, so this is treated as genuinely split.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the critique of consumerism and of needs manufactured by capitalism (Fromm on having versus being); self-sufficiency itself is not a stated aim.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: protection of communities against exploitation conflicts with opposition to exclusionary controls, and the sources do not address it.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: adherents back gender equality but were anti-militarist and critical of conscription, so they split; the sources do not address it.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from the humanist emphasis on universal human development and on estrangement from inherited forms, which makes national soil an unlikely focus.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The Praxis School defended free speech and civil liberties against Stalinist repression, and its ethics centre on human dignity, which excludes killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Not addressed by the humanist current, which rejected Soviet-style regimes without a stated line on China.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from its universalist, anti-nationalist humanism.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Marx's 1844 text treats private property as self-estrangement and communism as its positive abolition, which implies common claim on land and resources.

self-ownership.rationale: Adherents prize freedom and self-realisation but see property relations, including ownership of one's labour, as alienating; sources are not explicit.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred from the needs-based, anti-consumerist socialism; the sources do not discuss sales taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred from its view that people's needs should be met as of right for all.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The current rejects vanguard parties but favours self-managed councils and associations, so it would not have a leader bypass organised groups.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to capitalist power; privileges for connected firms are not discussed.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Marx's 1844 text treats religion as a form of estrangement, so it would not organise politics by denomination; this is inferred.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: it looks to future de-alienation, not revival of archaic values, though it criticises technology's domination of people.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to liberation and equal human agency; divorce law is not discussed.

national-resource-control.rationale: The Praxis School favoured social self-management over state or foreign control; no stated line on national control.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from its view that private property itself estranges people, so a voluntary process does not justify the result.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred from Johnson-Forest thinkers' attention to Black freedom struggles within the current; the sources do not state a position.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from its ethical stress on human agency and its defence of dissent against Party rule.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from Marx's view of free creative activity beyond alienated labour, though the humanist current also values meaningful work.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred: the 1844 Manuscripts ground estrangement in labour producing wealth, though humanists emphasise alienation more than value theory.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from its internationalism and critique of nationalist politics.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred from its focus on the whole person and alienation beyond wages, and Johnson-Forest attention to race and gender.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: It rejects vanguard-party rule and state capitalism and criticises market-driven manufactured needs, so both halves are rejected.

missingStatements.text: Under capitalism, relations between people take the form of relations between things, so that economic forces seem to rule human beings.
missingStatements.rationale: Reification, developed by Lukacs, is described as a central theme of Marxist humanism and is not captured by the existing alienation statement.

missingStatements.text: A socialist society should be judged by whether it frees people's creative activity, not only by who owns the means of production.
missingStatements.rationale: Fromm argues Marx would reject a state acting as capitalist employer, since his critique targeted the enslavement of people by their own creations.

notes: Strands differ: Johnson-Forest and Praxis writers hold workers' self-management and anti-vanguardism firmly, while Frankfurt-linked and existentialist writers are more ambivalent. Most statements on modern social issues are inferred.
